newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian govt presses early poll threat.
newsitem.headline: Australian govt presses early poll threat.

text.p: The Australian government on Tuesday added another policy to the pile of issues over which it is implicitly threatening an early election.

Training Minister David Kemp said that if the Senate blocked a plan to make some young people work for unemployment benefits, then the government would challenge the upper house to reject it again -- which would give Prime Minister John Howard a constitutional trigger for a snap election.

"Let me make it quite clear to the (opposition) Labor Party and to the Australian people, that if the Labor Party tries to destroy the work-for-the-dole scheme in the Senate then the government will put that legislation straight back into the Senate again," Kemp said.
Earlier on Tuesday Labor declared its intention to block another policy of the Liberal-National government, the sale of federal railway operator Australian National.
The government, elected last year for a three-year term, does not control the Senate and needs the backing of Labor, some minor parties or two independents to enact its policies.
But Howard last month called in the police to investigate fraud allegations against one of those independents, Mal Colston, and he is now withholding his vote.
The only other sources of the necessary votes are Labor, the Democrats or two Greens.
The Greens rarely agree with any government measures but Labor and, especially, the Democrats will often negotiate.
